sources.title: Vaccination against Lyme disease with recombinant Borrelia burgdorferi outer-surface lipoprotein A with adjuvant
sources.key_findings: Pivotal Phase III LYMErix (OspA) vaccine trial: ~76-80% reduction in new infections; transient arthralgia non-significantly increased; arthritis NOT increased versus placebo.
sources.relevance_notes: Primary evidence on the only licensed human Lyme vaccine and its (non-)arthritis safety signal.

sources.title: Identification of LFA-1 as a candidate autoantigen in treatment-resistant Lyme arthritis
sources.key_findings: Proposed molecular mimicry between B. burgdorferi OspA and human LFA-1 in HLA-DRB1*0401 individuals as a mechanism for treatment-resistant Lyme arthritis; basis of the OspA-vaccine autoimmunity concern.
sources.relevance_notes: The molecular-mimicry hypothesis (later not clinically confirmed) that drove fears about an OspA vaccine.

sources.title: The Lyme vaccine: a cautionary tale
sources.key_findings: LYMErix reduced infections ~80% yet was withdrawn within 3 years amid media coverage, side-effect fears, and falling sales rather than demonstrated harm.
sources.relevance_notes: Mainstream account that the withdrawal was a risk-perception cascade, not proven vaccine harm.

sources.title: The Rise and Fall of the Lyme Disease Vaccines: A Cautionary Tale for Risk Interventions in American Medicine and Public Health
sources.key_findings: Despite safety/efficacy in trials and postmarketing surveillance, the Lyme vaccines were withdrawn amid litigation and risk perception; a sociological analysis of the collapse.
sources.relevance_notes: Authoritative historical/sociological framing of why LYMErix failed.

sources.title: The year that shaped the outcome of the OspA vaccine for human Lyme disease
sources.key_findings: Reviews the 1998 FDA hearing and the OspA-LFA-1 molecular-mimicry concern, concluding the feared vaccine-induced autoimmunity was not borne out; informs next-generation design.
sources.relevance_notes: Mainstream retrospective on the OspA-autoimmunity concern and its resolution.

sources.title: Phase 3 VALOR Lyme Disease Trial (VLA15): primary vaccination series completion (Pfizer/Valneva)
sources.key_findings: VLA15, a six-valent OspA-based Lyme vaccine engineered to avoid the LFA-1-homologous region, completed its Phase 3 VALOR primary series (9,437 participants) in 2024.
sources.relevance_notes: Current OspA vaccine in development; signals the autoimmunity concern is considered manageable.

sources.title: Immunological and Antigenic Signatures Associated with Chronic Illnesses after COVID-19 Vaccination (Yale LISTEN)
sources.key_findings: Small cross-sectional study (42 PVS vs 22 controls) reporting altered T-cell profiles, EBV-reactivation serology, and circulating spike protein in post-vaccination-syndrome participants.
sources.relevance_notes: Serious but preliminary, unreplicated, non-Lyme-specific PVS research; flagged speculative/preprint.

sources.title: Investigation of Long COVID Prevalence and Its Relationship to Epstein-Barr Virus Reactivation
sources.key_findings: Long-COVID symptoms were associated with serological evidence of EBV reactivation, illustrating that immune challenges can reactivate latent pathogens.
sources.relevance_notes: Mainstream basis for the general 'immune event reactivates latent pathogen' mechanism (not Borrelia-specific).

sources.title: Posttreatment Lyme disease syndrome
sources.journal_or_publisher: Infectious Disease Clinics of North America
sources.key_findings: Characterizes PTLDS as a real post-infectious syndrome; provides the chronic-illness substrate that non-specific immune activation can transiently flare.
sources.relevance_notes: Anchors the immune-activation-flare and long-COVID/PTLDS-overlap framing.

sources.title: Antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis is associated with HLA-DR molecules that bind a Borrelia burgdorferi peptide
sources.key_findings: OspA-peptide-binding HLA-DR alleles mark antibiotic-refractory Lyme arthritis — the HLA/OspA axis underlying both the autoimmune-arthritis and vaccine-mimicry concerns.
sources.relevance_notes: Mechanistic bridge to Topic 1 and to the OspA-vaccine autoimmunity hypothesis.

sources.title: COVID-19 Vaccine Safety (CDC)
authors: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.journal_or_publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.key_findings: Summarizes the established safety profile of COVID-19 vaccines from large-scale surveillance; no established evidence of Borrelia reactivation.
sources.relevance_notes: Vaccine-safety consensus anchor for the misinformation-sensitive claims.

forum_excerpts.paraphrased_content: Posters with prior Lyme describe a symptom flare in the days to weeks after a COVID-19 vaccine dose, interpreting it as the vaccine worsening or 'waking up' their Lyme.
Many of the same posters report comparable or worse flares after COVID-19 infection itself, sometimes acknowledging the infection hit harder than the shot.
Stronger causal posts assert the COVID vaccine caused or reactivated active Lyme, often shared alongside broader anti-vaccine content.
Posters cite the withdrawn LYMErix vaccine as proof that Lyme vaccines harm people, extending the distrust to COVID and future Lyme (VLA15) vaccines.
A counter-current of posters report no flare or good vaccine tolerance, and some push back on causal claims and misinformation within the communities.
